title: Janapada of Pañcāla
capsule: Pañcāla occupied the upper Ganges-Yamuna Doab and Rohilkhand (modern Uttar Pradesh) and was, in the late Vedic and early Mahajanapada periods, among the most powerful states of northern India, listed in the Anguttara Nikaya as one of the sixteen great janapadas. Closely allied with the Kuru kingdom in earlier times, it rose to cultural and political prominence as Kuru declined, and split into a northern division centered on Ahichchhatra and a southern division centered on Kampilya. Its philosopher-king Pravahana Jaivali debated Brahmin scholars on Vedic doctrine, while its legendary ruler Drupada, father of Draupadi, figures centrally in the Mahabharata. The name is conventionally derived from a confederation of five (pañca) peoples.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Doab location and the two-capital division are textually secure; precise territorial limits, especially northern extent into the Himalayan foothills, are approximate reconstructions.
